svg.title: The ray bench: P1, P2 and P9
svg.desc: Top: the 4 KB height grid and a ray walking its cells toward the sun, with the cost model C_ray = C_setup + n C_step. Below, three panels: P1 cycles a ray against n with the predicted band and no measurements yet; P2 the same slice batched, interleaved with the vertex transform, and with the grid in OC-RAM; P9 the movers proxies against one slice. Foot: what each result feeds. Built as image ray1, not run on a console.
svg.text: The ray bench: three predictions to replace estimated cycle counts
BUILT, NOT RUN. ESTIMATE. Image psm-bench-ray1: host test 20,052 checks, 0 failed (x86); no console number yet. THESIS §6 P1, P2, P9.
Status: MEASURED our console · FACT a manual or our code · ESTIMATE our arithmetic or model · OPEN not known
What is timed: a ray walking a 4 KB height grid toward the sun (thesis §5.3)
64 x 64 cells, 1 B a cell (tallest caster,

A step: advance to the next x or z wall,
compare the cell's height with the ray's.
Stop at a hit, above H, or at the edge.
The model the bench must test
C_step 12 .. 16 cycles, C_setup about 30, grid in cache

What the bench feeds, once ray1 runs
P1 gives C_ray, which sets the slice k for a 2 ms budget (§5.9) and so the refresh period P = N / (k f) of §5.5.
P2 decides the frame's order: the slice in one batch before the transform (§5.10 step 2), or the grid in OC-RAM.
P9 decides whether the movers' proxies fit beside the slice, or need their own budget.
P3 (the shadow's lag at x60) waits on P1's rate. Every cycle count in §5 stays an ESTIMATE until P1, P2 and P9 replace it.
Stand-ins: random receivers (not the town's vertices), a synthetic 28,699-vertex stream, the real sun's 0.00465 rad; no two arrays a 16 KB multiple apart.
Kernel bytes were compared on x86 only: each page prints its own check; a BYTES DIFFER page keeps its times, but its kernel is not the reference.
